statement: A text string that does not hold the bytes for its declared length is not decoded, and the number of missing bytes is reported
deviation: Declared major type 3, ai 10 (a length-10 text string), and placed only 2 following bytes. **`normative_basis` changed (2026-08-09, req/38 §26 I-5)**: originally declared `IPLD-MUST`, but this was a mirror reading of A-8's (excess bytes) L66, not a verbatim one -- there is no truncation MUST anywhere in the IPLD spec text, and L66 is a sentence naming **excess** (measured at req/67 §2.6). A MUST-grade sentence naming a shortfall exists in RFC 8949 §3: "If the encoded sequence of bytes ends before the end of a data item, that item is not well-formed." (L487) + "A decoder **MUST NOT** return a decoded data item when it encounters input that is not a well-formed encoded CBOR data item" (L445-446). ∴ this vector's basis is correctly `RFC8949-MUST`; the old reading (the contrapositive of IPLD L66) was not wrong but was not verbatim, and is kept here on record. **The reason this one vector exists is the value of `missing`**: the 19 existing vectors do not reach `Truncated`, and even where one did, there was no assert reading the value (`req/58` §4 F-3's 2 survivors = the arithmetic of `take`'s `missing: end - self.b.len()`). The declared value is `end(11) - len(3) = 8`; changing `-` to `+` gives 14, and to `/` gives 3, both different from 8 -- a vector where the gap between length and remainder is small (e.g. `6261`) would let integer division coincide with the true value by chance, so a discriminating gap was chosen.
origin: gx self-authored for M3 hand 4 (req/38 §17 F-3's window)

control.note: A text string `"aa"` holding exactly its declared length. The only difference from the negative vector is the declared length; the byte count is the same, 3
